title: [YouPass Collect] - University choice factors in the UK in 1995 and 2005
prompt: The chart below shows the main reasons why students chose to study at a particular university in the UK in 1995 and 2005. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the percentages of students selecting five different reasons for choosing a university in the United Kingdom in 1995 and 2005.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while the majority of reasons saw an increase in importance over the period, two factors declined. In addition, suitable degree courses remained the most significant consideration in both years, while the proximity to parental homes experienced the most substantial growth.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the factors that increased, in 1995, suitable degree courses accounted for 35% of students' decisions, followed by quality of teaching at 15%, and close to parental home at just 10%. Over the decade, proximity to home rose most dramatically, more than doubling to around 22% by 2005. Meanwhile, suitable degree courses saw a modest increase to roughly 37%, maintaining its position as the leading factor, while quality of teaching similarly rose slightly to approximately 18%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the declining factors, good sport and social activities stood at 19% in 1995, slightly lower than quality of resources at 21%. However, the former experienced the most significant drop of any category, plummeting to just 6% by 2005, representing a decline of 13 percentage points. In contrast, quality of resources decreased more moderately, falling to around 17% at the end of the period.
